evidence.claim: MP Materials announced a public-private partnership with the Department of Defense to accelerate a US rare-earth magnet supply chain, including a planned second magnet manufacturing facility and a DoD NdPr price-floor commitment.
evidence.source_title: MP Materials Announces Transformational Public-Private Partnership with the Department of Defense to Accelerate U.S. Rare Earth Magnet Independence

evidence.claim: MP's 2025 annual filing states that it commissioned NdPr metal capabilities in 2024 and added strip-casting capabilities in 2025 to produce NdFeB alloy flake for magnet manufacturing.

USA Rare Earth closed its acquisition of Less Common Metals, described as a scaled ex-China rare-earth metal and alloy manufacturer with NdPr metal/alloy and strip-cast capability supporting USAR's Stillwater magnet facility.
evidence.source_title: USA Rare Earth Closes Acquisition of Less Common Metals

evidence.claim: USA Rare Earth says it is commissioning first-phase production at Stillwater, Oklahoma and targets 10,000 metric tons of annual magnet capacity at full capacity.

Energy Fuels announced that its high-purity dysprosium oxide passed initial QA/QC benchmarks for downstream permanent magnet production, following earlier news that its NdPr oxide had qualified for NdFeB magnet applications.
evidence.source_title: Energy Fuels' US-Produced Heavy Rare Earth Oxide Successfully Qualified for Use in Permanent Magnets

evidence.claim: NioCorp announced a DoD Defense Production Act Title III award expected to help establish a domestic scandium mine-to-master-alloy supply chain.

evidence.claim: Cached search context argues that the market may overcount non-Chinese NdFeB capacity because some nominal ex-China magnet capacity still depends on Chinese feedstock; the key variable is qualified non-Chinese oxide-to-magnet supply.

memory_update.text: MP is the reference benchmark for compliant US mine-to-magnet capacity because of explicit DoD partnership, NdPr price-floor support, and downstream metal/alloy/magnet buildout.
USAR should remain in the underfollowed lane because the Less Common Metals acquisition targets the metal/alloy/strip-cast chokepoint rather than only mining claims.
Energy Fuels is a second-order rare-earth magnet compliance candidate: monitor whether qualified NdPr and Dy oxides become recurring, compliant offtake into magnet supply chains.
NioCorp is speculative_shadow for this node: defense funding is real, but the direct rare-earth magnet-chain evidence is not yet strong enough without financing, production, and qualification proof.

Need a later pass on private/non-US-listed chokepoints such as Vulcan Elements, Neo Performance Materials, Lynas, Arnold Magnetic Technologies, Less Common Metals pre-acquisition history, and recycling/feedstock providers to map competitive pressure on US-listed candidates.

node: Non-Chinese-feedstock rare earth magnets and compliant magnet supply chains
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around compliant rare-earth magnet supply chains. The strongest direct reference name is MP Materials because it has an explicit DoD-backed mine-to-magnet pathway and NdPr price-floor support. The underfollowed lane is not generic rare-earth mining; it is companies that can document non-China oxide, metal/alloy, heavy rare-earth, recycling, or qualification pathways into NdFeB or other defense-relevant permanent magnets. USA Rare Earth and Energy Fuels are the most relevant underfollowed public-market candidates found in this pass; NioCorp is a speculative-shadow candidate because its rare-earth magnet exposure is less mature than its scandium/critical-minerals defense angle.
